hints: Focus on what controls how easily a halogenoalkane reacts, the strength and polarity of the carbon-halogen bond.
Compare fluorine and chlorine: fluorine is more electronegative and forms a shorter, stronger bond to carbon, so think about what that means for reactivity.
Now check the shape of $\text{CH}_3\text{CHF}_2$: with two very polar $\text{C-F}$ bonds on the same carbon, can the dipoles cancel out?
walkthrough:
**Check Statement 3 - Bond Strength**

Fluorine is small and very electronegative, so it forms a short, very strong bond to carbon. Chlorine is larger, so orbital overlap is poorer and the bond is longer and weaker.

Bond strength trend:
$$\text{C-F} > \text{C-Cl}$$

**Check Statement 1 - Reactivity**

Reactivity of halogenoalkanes in nucleophilic substitution depends on breaking the $\text{C-X}$ bond. A stronger bond needs more energy to break, so it reacts more slowly.

Since $\text{C-F}$ is stronger than $\text{C-Cl}$, $\text{CH}_3\text{CHF}_2$ is less reactive than $\text{CH}_3\text{CHCl}_2$. So statement 1 is correct.

**Check Statement 2 - Polarity**

The $\text{C-F}$ bond is very polar because fluorine is much more electronegative than carbon. In 1,1-difluoroethane, $\text{CH}_3\text{CHF}_2$, both $\text{C-F}$ dipoles are on the same carbon and point the same way.

They do not cancel, so the molecule has an overall dipole moment and is polar. So statement 2 is correct.

Since 1, 2 and 3 are all correct, the correct combination is 1, 2 and 3.

options.A: Correct. All three statements are true. C-F is stronger than C-Cl, so the fluoro compound is less reactive, and the two C-F dipoles make 1,1-difluoroethane polar.
options.B: Incorrect. This combination includes only 1 and 2. Statement 3 is also true because the small fluorine atom gives excellent overlap and a stronger C-F bond than C-Cl, so leaving it out is wrong.
options.C: Incorrect. This combination includes only 2 and 3. Statement 1 is also true because bond strength directly controls reactivity, and the stronger C-F bond makes the difluoro compound less reactive.
options.D: Incorrect. This combination includes only statement 1. Both statements 2 and 3 are also true, so choosing only one statement misses the polarity argument and the bond strength fact.
